overall: Council violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing off-purpose topics in two executive sessions and omitting the February 2011 session from its notice, but did not violate it on the reputation/character or April 2011 minutes-announcement claims; compliance order and member training certification issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the February 17, 2011 executive session on administrator contract talks drifted into competence, reputation and character without the employee present.
allegations.key_passage: the topics that were actually discussed should have been discussed in open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the February 17, 2011 executive session let discussion of the administrator's reputation and character proceed without the employee present or notified under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: However, we do not believe, as the complainant contends, that the Council engaged in any substantive discussion of the Administrator's reputation or character during this twenty-minute session, thus the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not affording the rights guaranteed under Purpose 1 to the Administrator.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the February 17, 2011 executive session was not listed in the meeting notice although the chair reasonably anticipated it at least 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: President Chirigotis therefore should have listed the executive session in the meeting notice before the February 17, 2011 meeting, or postponed the discussion until the topic could be included in a notice for a future meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the March 17, 2011 executive session on contract talks with the Town Manager turned to his professional competence and reputation and character.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the entire session should have been conducted in public.

allegations.summary: Complaint that members discussed the Town Manager's reputation and character at the March 17, 2011 executive session without the Purpose 1 rights being afforded.
allegations.key_passage: We do not believe, as the complainant contends, that the Council discussed the Town Manager's reputation or character during this session, thus the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not affording the rights guaranteed under Purpose 1 to the Town Manager.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the chair announced the March 17, 2011 executive session purpose without naming the Town Manager as the negotiating counterpart.
allegations.key_passage: President Chirigotis should therefore have stated that the Council was entering executive session to conduct contract negotiations with Town Manager Klimm.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Council failed to announce at its April 7, 2011 meeting its determination on release of the March 17, 2011 executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The Council had no legal obligation to inform the public of the purpose for continued non-disclosure of the March 17, 2011 executive session minutes at the April 7, 2011 meeting, therefore, because the Council had not yet undertaken a review of the minutes and no formal request for the minutes had been made.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the May 19, 2011 approval of the March 17 minutes did not state whether the executive session minutes would remain withheld.
allegations.key_passage: The May 19, 2011 minutes did not include a statement regarding the status of the March 17, 2011 executive session minutes, as required by G.L. c. 30A, § 22(g).

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Current Council members not present at the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law training must view the training video on the Attorney General's website.
Council to certify within 30 days of receiving the determination that all members have attended or reviewed an Attorney General Open Meeting Law training.
remedy_passage: We order the Council's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
